title: Did you know that neuroscience and scripture agree that you do not ha...
description: Did you know that neuroscience and scripture agree that you do not have to believe or act on every thought or feeling you have? Make this one move, and it will radically transform your life! I'm a neurosurgeon, but I'm also a trauma survivor and the father of a lost son. Throughout my career, and in my own life, the most helpful thing I've ever learned is that you can actually take command of what your mind and brain do when you experience, powerful and overwhelming thoughts and feelings. You don't have to be the hopeless, powerless patient who is waiting on someone to save you. You can make the patient – to– doctor switch, and modern neuroscience shows that your brain will almost immediately began to make structural changes to support your new, empowered position. You can take command of your physiology, improve your neurochemistry, be less anxious and overwhelmed. You can develop a purposeful approach to how you navigate your emotions, decisions, and your whole life. We call it self-brain surgery, but the Bible said it all along. II Corinthians 10:5 says to take every thought captive. Romans 12:2 says that God will renew your mind. Neuroscience shows that it happens almost instantly, once you change perspectives. In my New York Times best selling book,The Life-Changing Art of Self-Brain Surgery, I teach you how. Check the link in my bio to learn more. Share this with a friend who feels overwhelmed, and save it for the next time you need to remember that you already have everything you need to make the switch. Follow me for daily connections between neuroscience and scripture.

title: People think they have a willpower problem. Most of the time, what th...
description: People think they have a willpower problem. Most of the time, what they actually have is an automation problem. As a neurosurgeon, I’ve spent decades watching brains change after injury. As a trauma survivor, I’ve lived through the painstaking work of changing my own. As someone who believes the Bible and modern neuroscience point in the same direction, I’ve learned this: You don’t become what you want. You become what you repeatedly think, believe, and practice. Every thought you rehearse strengthens a pathway. Every reaction you repeat becomes easier to repeat again. Your brain is always wiring itself around whatever your mind repeatedly gives attention to. That’s why motivation fades. That’s why resolutions fail. That’s why you keep ending up in the same emotional place. You don’t rise to your intentions. You default to what you're rehearsing in your neural patterns. The good news? The same neuroplasticity that built the patterns keeping you stuck can build new ones that set you free. You're not doomed to stay the same forever if you're willing to renew your mind (Ephesians 4:23) Transformation isn’t magic. It’s biology directed by belief. It’s neuroscience aligned with truth. It’s Self-Brain Surgery. And the hard truth is: nothing changes until you change something. And you can't change your life until you change your mind. The question isn’t whether your brain is changing. The question is: Who is directing the change? Check out my new book, The Life-Changing Art of Self-Brain Surgery to learn more, and follow me for daily lessons from neuroscience and scripture.  They call me the "Bible+Brain Guy," but I'm not doing this just because I'm a brain surgeon; it's how I got unstuck from PTSD and losing my son. And I want that for you too.  Being unable to change your own life hurts, and changing your mind will get you moving again. title: Unpopular opinion: you are not stuck because of someone or something ...
description: Unpopular opinion: you are not stuck because of someone or something outside of you. You're stuck because you keep thinking about the same things from the same perspective. Neuroscience studies show that about 90% of the thoughts you think every day are the same set of things you thought about the day before. And since other studies show that a huge percentage of our automatic thoughts and feelings are negative and/or false, that means you're spending most of your thought life pondering things that are inaccurate, improbable, or otherwise untrue. And since we know that neuroplasticity (the way your brain changes its structure every day)happens mostly in response to what we think about, that means most of the time you're building a brain that's trying to navigate a world based on your worries and fears rather than on what's true and possible for you. That's why you feel stuck, but I have good news: You don't have to stay that way.  You can change your brain from a fear-based survival machine to an opportunity-based "thrival" engine. (Yes, that's a made-up word) I call it self-brain surgery, and it starts by implementing II Corinthians 10:5- "We take every thought captive." The science is clear: change the character of your thinking and your brain will rewire to show you a more hopeful world. And you can do it, because you have a sound mind (II Timothy 1:7). Check out my latest book, The Life-Changing Art of Self-Brain Surgery to learn more, and follow me for daily lessons from neuroscience and scripture.  They call me the "Bible+Brain Guy," but I'm not doing this just because I'm a brain surgeon; it's how I got unstuck from PTSD and losing my son. And I want that for you too.  Being stuck in your own life hurts, and changing your mind will get you moving again. description: Sometimes the most powerful thing you can do is nothing. A deep breath. A short prayer. A quiet decision to try again tomorrow. title: This is a high-grade glioma, known as glioblastoma multiforme or GBM....
description: This is a high-grade glioma, known as glioblastoma multiforme or GBM.  How do you think it was treated: 1. Surgery to remove the tumor 2. Biopsy followed by radiation and chemotherapy  3. Surgery, chemo, and radiation  (Scroll to the bottom for the answer) Glioblastoma is one of the most aggressive brain cancers. It's fast, relentless, and devastating. 💔 I’ve treated it many times, and it never gets easier. 🧠 Median survival is just 12–15 months. 📊 Less than 5% survive 5 years. Treatment usually includes surgery, radiation, and temozolomide, a chemo drug that can help, but it’s not a cure. We’re also seeing hope in things like Tumor Treating Fields, immunotherapy, and clinical trials. 🙏 But here’s what I’ll never forget: I’ve learned more from glioblastoma patients and their families about what really matters—grit, resilience, faith, and hope—than I ever did in medical school. My book "I've Seen the End of You" tells many of the stories of these brave patients and their families. July 17 was Glioblastoma awareness day, and I want to remind you about this important disease and the incredible people who are facing it, those who love someone who's fighting it, and all those who are searching for a cure. #glioblastoma #braincancer #temozolomide #neurosurgery #hope #faith #selfbrainsurgery #thedrleewarrenpodcast #neuroscience #neurosurgeon  (This tumor was biopsied using computer guidance, because it is too deep in the brain to remove safely. After the diagnosis was confirmed with biopsy, the patient received fractionated radiotherapy and oral chemotherapy)

description: 🧠Upstream from every decision and reaction we make in response to the thoughts, emotions, and circumstances we have, there is a river of factors like genetics, epigenetic starting points, upbringing, and prior trauma/tragedy/etc.  🧠These things flow into our minds and instantly color things we think about NOW, but they blend so seamlessly into our consciousness that, unless we are careful to examine them (II Corinthians 10:5), they will feel like they are a part of what’s happening in the current situation. 🧠 If we react to them as if they’re currently real, then they blend into our reality and flow downstream, mixing into the rest of our lives and soaking into the lives of everyone we interact with.  ✝️🧠❤️ If we learn to biopsy our thoughts and feelings, we can take action on what we experience as it is, and understand that what’s happened in the past can refine us (Isaiah 48:10), but if doesn’t have to DEFINE us.  🧠 The neuroscience works in our favor here: your brain is designed to heal, and the healing starts with renewing our minds (Romans 12:2).  🧠 Love your downstream life more than you’re drowned by what came before. You can change! You can be healed! You’re not stuck. #selfbrainsurgery
